# Introduction

**vayuayan** (वायुअयन) is an R package for fetching and analyzing air quality data from multiple sources in India. The name combines two Sanskrit words:

- **Vayu** (वायु): Wind, air
- **Ayan** (अयन): Path, journey, movement

Together, "Vayuayan" means "the path of wind" - representing the journey and movement of air quality data across space and time.

## Installation

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# Install from GitHub
devtools::install_github("saketlab/vayuayan-r")
```

## Data Sources

The package provides access to:

1. **CPCB India**: Central Pollution Control Board monitoring network
   - Historical AQI data
   - Real-time monitoring data
   - Station-level and city-level data

2. **WUSTL ACAG**: Washington University satellite PM2.5 data
   - Global coverage
   - Monthly and annual data
   - High-resolution gridded data

## Quick Start

```{r quickstart}
library(vayuayan)

# Display welcome message with quick start guide
vayuayan_welcome()
```

# Historical AQI Data

The `CPCBHistorical` class provides access to historical air quality data from the Central Pollution Control Board.

## Exploring Available Data

```{r historical_explore}
# Initialize client
historical <- CPCBHistorical$new()

# Get list of states
states <- historical$get_state_list()
head(states)

# Get cities in Maharashtra
cities <- historical$get_city_list("Maharashtra")
head(cities)

# Get monitoring stations in Mumbai
stations <- historical$get_station_list("Mumbai")
head(stations)
```

## Downloading Historical Data

### City-Level Data

```{r city_data}
# Download city-level AQI data for Mumbai in 2024
historical$download_city_data(
  city = "Mumbai",
  year = 2024,
  save_location = "mumbai_aqi_2024.csv"
)
```

### Station-Level Data

```{r station_data}
# Download station-level data
historical$download_station_data(
  station_id = "site_5964",
  year = 2024,
  save_location = "station_data_2024.csv"
)
```

# Live AQI Monitoring

The `CPCBLive` class enables real-time air quality monitoring.

## Location-Based Monitoring

```{r live_location}
# Initialize live monitoring client
live <- CPCBLive$new()

# Get your current location (IP-based)
location <- live$get_system_location()
print(location)

# Find nearest monitoring station
nearest <- live$get_nearest_station()
cat("Nearest Station:", nearest$station_name)
cat("Distance:", round(nearest$distance_km, 2), "km")
```

## Getting Live AQI Data

```{r live_aqi}
# Get live AQI data for nearest station
aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data()

# Display pollutant metrics
if (!is.null(aqi_data$metrics)) {
  for (metric in aqi_data$metrics) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: Avg=%s, Min=%s, Max=%s\n",
                metric$name, metric$avg, metric$min, metric$max))
  }
}

# Get AQI for specific coordinates
mumbai_coords <- c(19.0760, 72.8777)
aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data(coords = mumbai_coords)

# Get historical live data (specific date and hour)
aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data(
  station_id = "site_5964",
  date = "2024-02-25",
  hour = 10
)
```

# Data Analysis with tidyverse

The package integrates seamlessly with tidyverse workflows.

## Station Data Analysis

```{r tidyverse_analysis}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Get all station data
live <- CPCBLive$new()
all_stations <- live$get_all_india()

# Convert to tidy dataframe
df <- stations_to_dataframe(all_stations)

# State-wise summary
state_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(state_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_stations = n(),
    live_stations = sum(live),
    offline_stations = sum(!live),
    avg_aqi = mean(avg_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(live_stations))

print(head(state_summary, 10))
```

## AQI Distribution Analysis

```{r aqi_distribution}
# Analyze AQI distribution
df_with_categories <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_aqi)) %>%
  mutate(aqi_category = get_aqi_categories(avg_aqi))

# Category distribution
category_dist <- df_with_categories %>%
  count(aqi_category) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

print(category_dist)

# Visualize AQI distribution
ggplot(df_with_categories, aes(x = avg_aqi, fill = aqi_category)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Good" = "green",
      "Satisfactory" = "lightgreen",
      "Moderate" = "yellow",
      "Poor" = "orange",
      "Very Poor" = "red",
      "Severe" = "darkred"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of AQI Values Across India",
    x = "AQI",
    y = "Number of Stations",
    fill = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# PM2.5 Satellite Data

The `PM25Client` class processes satellite-based PM2.5 data from WUSTL ACAG.

## Basic Usage

```{r pm25_basic}
# Initialize PM2.5 client
pm25 <- PM25Client$new(cache_dir = "pm25_cache")

# Get PM2.5 statistics for a region (requires GeoJSON file)
delhi_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(
  geojson_file = "delhi_ncr.geojson",
  year = 2023,
  month = 11
)

print(delhi_stats)
# Output: List with mean, std, min, max PM2.5 values
```

## Grouped Analysis

```{r pm25_grouped}
# Analyze PM2.5 grouped by state
state_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(
  geojson_file = "india_districts.geojson",
  year = 2023,
  month = 11,
  group_by = "state_name"
)

print(head(state_stats))

# Analyze with multiple grouping columns
district_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(
  geojson_file = "india_districts.geojson",
  year = 2023,
  month = 11,
  group_by = "state_name,district_name"
)
```

## Cache Management

```{r pm25_cache}
# List cached NetCDF files
pm25$list_cached_files()

# Clear cache to free disk space
pm25$clear_cache()

# Force re-download of data
pm25$download_netcdf_if_needed(
  year = 2023,
  month = 11,
  force_download = TRUE
)
```

# Geospatial Analysis

## Mapping Monitoring Stations

```{r geospatial}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# Get station data
live <- CPCBLive$new()
all_stations <- live$get_all_india()
df <- stations_to_dataframe(all_stations)

# Filter live stations with valid coordinates
live_stations <- df %>%
  filter(live == TRUE, !is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) %>%
  mutate(aqi_category = get_aqi_categories(avg_aqi))

# Convert to spatial object
stations_sf <- st_as_sf(
  live_stations,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)

# Plot stations on map
ggplot(stations_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = aqi_category), size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Good" = "green",
      "Satisfactory" = "lightgreen",
      "Moderate" = "yellow",
      "Poor" = "orange",
      "Very Poor" = "red",
      "Severe" = "darkred"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Live Air Quality Monitoring Stations in India",
    subtitle = paste("Total stations:", nrow(stations_sf)),
    color = "AQI Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Spatial Filtering

```{r spatial_filtering}
# Find stations within a specific region (Maharashtra)
mh_bbox <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = 72.5, ymin = 15.5, xmax = 80.5, ymax = 22.5),
  crs = 4326
)

mh_stations <- st_crop(stations_sf, mh_bbox)

cat("Stations in Maharashtra region:", nrow(mh_stations))
```

# Utility Functions

## Station Name Cleaning

```{r clean_names}
# Clean station names for file naming
clean_station_name("Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range, Delhi - DPCC")
# Output: "Dr_Karni_Singh_Shooting_Range_Delhi_DPCC"

clean_station_name("ITO, Delhi - DPCC")
# Output: "ITO_Delhi_DPCC"
```

## Distance Calculations

```{r distance}
# Calculate distance between two locations (km)
mumbai <- c(19.0760, 72.8777)
delhi <- c(28.7041, 77.1025)

distance <- haversine_distance(
  mumbai[1], mumbai[2],
  delhi[1], delhi[2]
)

cat("Distance from Mumbai to Delhi:", round(distance), "km")
```

## Comprehensive Analysis

```{r comprehensive}
# Comprehensive station analysis
live <- CPCBLive$new()
all_stations <- live$get_all_india()

analysis <- analyze_station_data(all_stations)

# View analysis results
str(analysis)
```

# Best Practices

## Error Handling

```{r error_handling}
# Always use tryCatch for API calls
tryCatch({
  live <- CPCBLive$new()
  aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data()
  print(aqi_data$metrics)
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Error fetching data: ", e$message)
})
```

## Caching Strategy

```{r caching}
# Use a consistent cache directory
pm25 <- PM25Client$new(cache_dir = "~/.vayuayan_cache")

# Check cache before downloading
cached_files <- pm25$list_cached_files()

# Clear old cache periodically
if (length(cached_files) > 10) {
  pm25$clear_cache()
}
```

## Data Validation

```{r validation}
# Validate data before analysis
df <- stations_to_dataframe(all_stations)

# Check for missing coordinates
stations_no_coords <- df %>%
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude))

if (nrow(stations_no_coords) > 0) {
  warning(sprintf(
    "%d stations missing coordinates",
    nrow(stations_no_coords)
  ))
}

# Check for unrealistic AQI values
df %>%
  filter(avg_aqi < 0 | avg_aqi > 500) %>%
  nrow() -> invalid_aqi

if (invalid_aqi > 0) {
  warning(sprintf("%d stations with invalid AQI", invalid_aqi))
}
```

# Conclusion

The vayuayan package provides comprehensive tools for:

- Accessing historical and real-time air quality data
- Processing satellite-based PM2.5 measurements
- Performing geospatial analysis of monitoring networks
- Integrating with tidyverse workflows

For more information:

- Package documentation: `?vayuayan`
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/saketlab/vayuayan-r
- Report issues: https://github.com/saketlab/vayuayan-r/issues
